chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from al-Ash'ari, from Samakah ibn Mihran, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Verily, Allah, the Exalted, did not send any Prophet or Imam except that he is the most knowledgeable of the people regarding Allah's affairs, the best in executing them, and the most perceptive of them.'

He said: 'And He does not command them except with what Allah commands them, nor forbids them except with what Allah forbids them, nor do they take upon themselves except what Allah has taken upon them, nor do they learn except what Allah has taught them, nor do they acquire deep understanding (fiqh) except in what Allah has made them understand, nor do they acquire deep understanding except in what Allah has obligated upon them.'

He said: 'If that is so, then verily Allah, the Exalted, has made for you in His Book a guide and a light, and has made for you in it a clarification and detail, and has made for you in it the permissible and the forbidden, and has made for you in it a Sunnah and an obligation, and has made for you in it a command and a prohibition, and has made for you in it a decree and a determination, and has made for you in it knowledge and action, and has made for you in it a religion and a world, and has made for you in it an Hereafter and a world, and has made for you in it Paradise and Hellfire, and has made for you in it an admonition and a reminder, and has made for you in it a proof and a clarification, and has made for you in it a guide and a light.'

He said: 'Whoever follows the Book of Allah, and follows the Sunnah of His Messenger, and takes hold of Allah's affair, and is with Allah, will be with Allah, and will be with Allah, and will be with Allah.'

key_terms.أَمْرُ اللَّهِ: Affairs of Allah (divine commands and decrees)
key_terms.فَقِهَ: To acquire deep understanding (specifically in religious law)

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between the knowledge of the Imams and the Quran according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq utilizes this hadith to establish the doctrine of *Ismah* (infallibility) and the continuity of divine guidance through the Ahl al-Bayt, asserting that the Imams possess the complete, uncorrupted understanding of the Quran. This underscores the Shia view that the Quran's explicit laws (*zahir*) are complemented by the Imams' authoritative interpretation (*ta'wil*), ensuring that the community retains access to all necessary religious knowledge without need for further revelation.
